title: 1996 AHSME Problem 18
statement: A circle of radius \(2\) has center at \((2,0).\) A circle of radius \(1\) has center at \((5,0).\) A line is tangent to the two circles at points in the first quadrant. Which of the following is closest to the \(y\)-intercept of the line?

solutions.text: Write the upper common tangent as \(mx-y+b=0\) and let \(s=\sqrt{m^2+1}.\) The two center-to-line distances give \[ 2m+b=2s,\qquad 5m+b=s. \] Thus \(3m=-s,\) so \(9m^2=m^2+1\) and \(m=-\frac{1}{\sqrt8}.\) From the second equation, \[ \begin{aligned} b&=s-5m\\ &=\frac3{\sqrt8}+\frac5{\sqrt8}=2\sqrt2. \end{aligned} \] Therefore the correct answer is D.
hints: Write the tangent as \(y=mx+b\) and use point-to-line distance for each center
Subtract the two distance equations to determine the slope before solving for the intercept
